title: Times tables to 12
objectives: Recall every product up to 12 by 12 without counting up
Rebuild a forgotten fact from the patterns of the 9, 11 and 12 rows
Use symmetry to cut the 144 cells to 78 facts

screens.prose: This is the times table up to 12 by 12. Each cell is its row number times its column number.
screens.question: Shade every cell in the table equal to 24.

hints.text: Which pairs of numbers up to 12 multiply to 24?
3 × 8 is one pair. Its mirror, 8 × 3, is another cell.
The pairs are 2 and 12, 3 and 8, 4 and 6. Shade each pair both ways round.

feedback.correct: Six cells hold 24: three pairs, each shown both ways round.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. List every pair that multiplies to 24, then find each pair both ways round.

byKey.one-side: You found 2 × 12, 3 × 8 and 4 × 6. Each also appears the other way round, below the diagonal.
byKey.other-side: You found 12 × 2, 8 × 3 and 6 × 4. Each also appears the other way round, above the diagonal.
byKey.r4c5: 4 × 5 is 20, not 24. Check each shaded cell again.
byKey.r5c5: 5 × 5 is 25, not 24. Check each shaded cell again.
byKey.r3c9: 3 × 9 is 27, not 24. Check each shaded cell again.
byKey.r2c11: 2 × 11 is 22, not 24. Check each shaded cell again.

explain.text: 24 shows up six times: 2 × 12, 3 × 8 and 4 × 6, each both ways round. The table is a mirror image across its diagonal. So its 144 cells hold only 78 different facts.

canvas.caption: The mirror line runs down the diagonal

screens.prose: Here is the 9 row on its own. Add the digits of each product: 18 gives 1 + 8.
screens.question: Tap the one product whose digits do not add up to 9.

hints.text: Work along the row: 9, then 1 + 8, then 2 + 7.
Most products give 9. One of them gives 9 + 9.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add the digits of each product in turn.

byKey.r1c12: 108 gives 1 + 0 + 8 = 9, so it fits the pattern.
byKey.r1c1: 9 is a single digit, and it is 9, so it fits.

explain.text: Each step adds 9, one ten up and one unit down. From 9 to 90 that keeps the digit sum at 9. At 99 the sum is 18, still a multiple of 9.

screens.prose: You saw each step add a ten and take away a unit. That is the **nines pattern**: $9 \times n = 10n - n$, ten lots minus one lot. This row has two slips in it.
screens.question: Tap the two products that are wrong.

hints.text: Test each product as ten lots minus one lot.
Look hard at 9 × 7 and 9 × 12.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Test each product as ten lots minus one lot.

byKey.flagged-99: You flagged 99 because its digits make 18. But $9 \times 11 = 110 - 11 = 99$, so it is right. Look at 118 instead.
byKey.missed-62: You flagged 99, which is right, and missed 62. $9 \times 7 = 70 - 7 = 63$.
byKey.r1c11: 99 is right: $110 - 11 = 99$. Its digit sum is 18, which is still a multiple of 9.

explain.text: Ten lots minus one lot checks any product in the row. $9 \times 7 = 70 - 7 = 63$ and $9 \times 12 = 120 - 12 = 108$. The digit sum also caught both slips, but it fails on 99, so trust $10n - n$.

screens.prose: Now the 11 row. Up to 11 × 9 it repeats the digit. Past that, think of 11 lots as ten lots plus one lot.
screens.question: What is 11 × 12?

hints.text: What is 10 × 12?
The cell before is 11 × 11 = 121. One more step along the row adds 11.
Ten lots of 12 is 120. One more lot of 12 makes 132.

feedback.correct: Ten twelves and one more twelve: 120 + 12 = 132.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work out ten lots of 12, then add one more lot.

byKey.repeat: You wrote 12 twice, as for 11 × 3 = 33. That works only for one-digit numbers.
byKey.plus-one: That is 11 × 11. You need one more step along the row, which adds 11.
byKey.plus-twelve: You added 12 to 121. But 121 is 11 × 11, and each step along the row adds 11.

explain.text: $11 \times 12 = 10 \times 12 + 12 = 132$. The repeated digit is the same idea: $11 \times 7 = 70 + 7 = 77$. Ten lots plus one lot works all along the row.

screens.prose: Twelve lots is ten lots plus two lots. The top two rows give those parts for every number.
screens.question: What is 12 × 8?

hints.text: Read the two cells above the question mark.

byKey.tens-only: That is ten lots of 8. Two more lots add 16.
byKey.side-by-side: You wrote 80 and 16 side by side. Add them instead: 80 + 16.

explain.text: Column 8 holds 80 and 16, and together they make 96. Any 12s fact is a 10s fact plus a doubled fact. That turns the hardest row into two easy ones.

screens.prose: The facts people mix up most sit in the middle of the table. There, 48, 54, 56 and 63 crowd together.
screens.question: Shade every cell equal to 56.

hints.text: Which two numbers up to 12 multiply to 56?
Read 5, 6, 7, 8 in order: 56 = 7 × 8.
7 × 8 and 8 × 7 both give 56. No other cell does.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the pair that makes 56, then shade it both ways round.

byKey.fifty-four: You shaded 6 × 9 and 9 × 6, which make 54. 56 is 7 × 8: read 5, 6, 7, 8 in order.
byKey.r6c9: You shaded 6 × 9, which is 54. Its neighbour 56 is 7 × 8.
byKey.r9c6: You shaded 9 × 6, which is 54. Its neighbour 56 is 8 × 7.
byKey.one-way: You shaded 7 × 8. Its mirror, 8 × 7, is 56 too.
byKey.other-way: You shaded 8 × 7. Its mirror, 7 × 8, is 56 too.
byKey.r8c8: 8 × 8 is 64. Take one 8 away and you reach 56.
byKey.r7c7: 7 × 7 is 49. Add one more 7 and you reach 56.
byKey.r6c8: 6 × 8 is 48. Add one more 8 and you reach 56.

explain.text: 56 appears only as 7 × 8 and 8 × 7. Its neighbours 48, 54 and 63 are 6 × 8, 6 × 9 and 7 × 9. When a middle fact feels shaky, rebuild it from one you trust: $7 \times 7 + 7 = 56$.

screens.prose: You rebuilt facts from round numbers and from their mirrors. As rules, for any whole number $n$: $$9n = 10n - n \qquad 11n = 10n + n \qquad 12n = 10n + 2n$$ And $a \times b = b \times a$ cuts the table from 144 cells to 78 facts.
screens.question: Which working builds 9 × 12 from facts you trust?

options.why: You took nine tens and added one 12. By the 12s rule, $12 \times 9 = 90 + 18$.
You took 9 off ten twelves. One lot is a whole 12, so take off 12.
You started from $9 \times 11 = 99$ and added 12. One more step adds a 9, giving 108.

hints.text: Nine lots is ten lots minus one lot.
Ten lots of 12 is 120. Take off one lot of 12.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Nine lots is ten lots minus one lot.

explain.text: $9 \times 12 = 10 \times 12 - 12 = 108$. You could also go $12 \times 9 = 90 + 18$, by the 12s rule. Both routes meet, because $a \times b = b \times a$.

screens.prose: Why does the nines pattern work? Build $9 \times 8$ from facts you are sure of, with a reason for each line.
screens.question: Put the lines in order.

hints.text: Which line still has the 9 in it?
The bracket has to be written before it is multiplied out.
Rewrite 9, multiply out, name the two products, subtract.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Start from the line that rewrites 9.

byKey.spread: That line multiplies out a bracket. Write the bracket first.
byKey.name: That line names the two products. They come from multiplying out the bracket.
byKey.finish: That is the answer, so it comes last.

explain.text: Writing 9 as $10 - 1$ turns one hard product into two easy ones. Multiplying each part by 8 is the step you used along the row. The same four lines work for any $9n$.

screens.prose: Your trade log shows three buys this morning. A trade's value is its number of shares times its price.
screens.question: Fill in each value and the total, in pounds.

hints.text: Each value is one fact from the table.
7 × 8 = 56, 9 × 12 = 108 and 12 × 11 = 132. Then add the three.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply shares by price for each trade, then add the three values.

byKey.r0c3: 7 × 8 is 56. Rebuild it from 7 × 7 = 49 if it feels shaky.
byKey.r1c3: 9 × 12 is ten twelves minus one twelve: 120 − 12 = 108.
byKey.r2c3: 12 × 11 is ten elevens plus two elevens: 110 + 22 = 132.

explain.text: Each value is one fact from the table: 56, 108 and 132. Together they make £296.00. A quick product like this lets you check a fill before it settles.

ideas: The table is a mirror image across its diagonal, so 144 cells hold only 78 different facts.
Rebuild a row from round numbers: $9n = 10n - n$, $11n = 10n + n$ and $12n = 10n + 2n$.
When a middle fact feels shaky, step from a neighbour you trust: $7 \times 8 = 7 \times 7 + 7$.

formula.name: The nines pattern
formula.note: Ten lots minus one lot. The digits of $9n$ add to a multiple of 9.

summary.trap: 7 × 8 is 56, and 6 × 9 is 54. Read 5, 6, 7, 8 in order: $56 = 7 \times 8$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Step from a fact you trust, such as 7 × 7 = 49.

byKey.fifty-four: That is 6 × 9. 8 × 7 is 56: read 5, 6, 7, 8 in order.
byKey.six-eights: That is 6 × 8, one eight short. Add 8 more.
byKey.eight-eights: That is 8 × 8, one eight too many. Take 8 away.

options.why: You took 2 off 120 instead of 12. One lot of 12 comes off: $120 - 12 = 108$.
That is 8 × 12, one twelve too few.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work out ten lots of 12, then take off one lot.

explain.text: $10 \times 12 = 120$, and one lot of 12 comes off. $120 - 12 = 108$.

quiz.prose: Use the 12s rule: ten lots plus two lots.
quiz.question: What is 12 × 7?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add ten sevens and two sevens.

byKey.one-lot: That is 11 × 7. Twelve lots is ten lots plus two lots, so add 14.
byKey.side-by-side: You wrote 7 tens and 14 side by side. Add 70 and 14 instead.
byKey.tens-only: That is ten sevens. Two more sevens add 14.

quiz.prose: The 12 by 12 table has 144 cells. You use $a \times b = b \times a$ so that you learn each pair only once.
quiz.question: How many different facts are left to learn?

feedback.correct: 12 squares on the diagonal, plus half of the other 132 cells.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. The diagonal cells have no mirror partner. Count them apart from the rest.

byKey.halved: You halved 144. But the 12 squares on the diagonal, such as 7 × 7, have no mirror partner.
byKey.all: That counts 3 × 8 and 8 × 3 as two facts. They are one fact learned once.
byKey.no-diagonal: You left out the squares on the diagonal. 7 × 7 is a fact you still need.

explain.text: The diagonal holds 12 squares, each its own mirror. The other 132 cells pair up into 66 facts. That makes $12 + 66 = 78$.
